questions.question_text:
A vacuum cleaner can be bought on terms for a $\$90$ deposit and $15$ monthly instalments of $\$46.20$.
What is the total amount paid on terms?

options.why: Added up the $15$ instalments but left the $\$90$ deposit out of the total.
Used $12$ instalments instead of the $15$ stated in the question.
Subtracted the deposit from the instalment total instead of adding it.

questions.question_text:
A bed frame costs $\$980$ cash, or a $\$140$ deposit and $16$ monthly instalments of $\$59.50$.
How much more than the cash price is paid by buying on terms?

options.why: Gave the total paid on terms instead of the amount above the cash price.
Left the deposit out of the total, then subtracted $\$952$ from the cash price.
Used $18$ instalments instead of the $16$ stated in the question.

questions.question_text:
A coffee machine costs $\$850$ cash, or a $\$150$ deposit and $12$ monthly instalments of $\$65$.
How much would be saved by paying cash?

options.why: Gave the total paid on terms instead of subtracting the cash price.
Left out the deposit, then subtracted the instalment total of $\$780$ from the cash price.
Added the deposit twice before subtracting the cash price.

questions.question_text:
A pressure washer has a cash price of $\$1\,250$.
On terms it costs a $20\%$ deposit and $18$ monthly instalments of $\$63.40$.
What is the total amount paid on terms?

options.why: Added the instalments only and left the $\$250$ deposit out of the total.
Took the $20\%$ deposit from the instalment total instead of from the cash price.
Added the $\$1000$ balance owing to the instalments instead of the deposit.

questions.question_text:
A used hatchback is advertised at $\$6\,500$.
On terms, a $\$1\,500$ deposit is paid and the balance is repaid over $2$ years with simple interest charged at $9\%$ p.a. on the balance owing.
What is the total cost of buying the car on terms?

options.why: Gave the balance owing plus interest and left the deposit out of the total.
Charged the interest on the full $\$6500$ cash price instead of on the balance owing.
Used $1$ year instead of the $2$-year term in the interest calculation.

questions.question_text:
After the deposit on a home office desk is paid, the balance owing including interest is $\$2\,376$.
It is repaid in $24$ equal monthly repayments over $2$ years.
Each monthly repayment, to the nearest cent, is:

options.why: Divided by $12$ months instead of by the $24$ repayments in the term.
Used $26$ repayments rather than $24$, then rounded to the nearest cent.
Divided by the $2$-year term rather than by the number of repayments.

questions.question_text:
A jacket costing $\$186$ is paid for using an interest-free buy now, pay later scheme in $4$ equal instalments.
The size of each instalment is:

options.why: Divided by the $3$ remaining instalments, forgetting the one paid at purchase.
Halved the price instead of dividing it into $4$ equal instalments.
Multiplied the price by $4$ instead of dividing it by $4$.

questions.question_text:
An order costing $\$64$ is paid for using an interest-free buy now, pay later scheme in $4$ equal instalments.
A missed payment incurs an initial late fee of $\$10$ and a further fee of up to $\$7$ if it remains unpaid $7$ days later.
Total late fees are capped at the lower of $25\%$ of the order value or $\$68$.
The initial fee has already been charged. What further late fee is charged after $7$ days?

options.why: Charged the further fee in full without allowing for the total late fee cap.
Gave the maximum total late fees instead of subtracting the initial fee already charged.
Calculated $25\%$ of one $\$16$ instalment instead of using the order value and subtracting the initial fee.

questions.solution_text:
Late fee cap:
$25\%\times\$64=\$16$
Since $\$16$ is less than $\$68$, the cap is $\$16$.
Amount remaining under the cap:
$\$16-\$10=\$6$
The further late fee is reduced from $\$7$ to $\$6.00$.

questions.question_text:
An order costing $\$360$ is bought using an interest-free buy now, pay later scheme.
The maximum total late fees are the lower of $25\%$ of the order value or $\$68$.
What is the maximum amount payable in late fees?

options.why: Calculated $25\%$ of the order value but ignored the lower cap of $\$68$.
Added one initial fee of $\$10$ and one further fee of $\$7$ instead of finding the maximum total late fees.
Applied $25\%$ to one quarter of the order value instead of to the whole order.

questions.solution_text:
$25\%\times\$360=\$90$
Since $\$68$ is less than $\$90$, the maximum amount payable in late fees is $\$68.00$.

questions.question_text:
A laundry package costs $\$4\,850$ cash.
It is bought on terms with a $\$850$ deposit, and the balance is repaid over $3$ years in $36$ equal monthly repayments with simple interest charged at $10.5\%$ p.a. on the balance owing.
What is each monthly repayment, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Included the deposit in the amount divided between the monthly repayments, although it was already paid.
Charged interest on the full cash price rather than on the balance after the deposit.
Used $1$ year rather than $3$ years when calculating the interest.

questions.solution_text:
Balance owing:
$\$4\,850-\$850=\$4\,000$
Interest on the balance:
$I=Prn$
$=\$4\,000\times0.105\times3$
$=\$1\,260$
Total owing:
$\$4\,000+\$1\,260=\$5\,260$
Monthly repayment:
$\$5\,260\div36\approx\$146.11$
